reasons: Both answers say clearly that the model swap is not enough. Both also give per-test attempt limits, repeat detection, git commit and rollback against regressions, protection of the test files, and the idea of escalating to Opus, all in Russian with Python code. B's skeleton puts every stopping condition the rubric asks for into one runnable loop: a global MAX_ITERS, a dollar budget, a NO_PROGRESS_LIMIT counter, a pytest timeout and a final report. A has no global iteration cap and no failing-count progress check, and its wall-clock limit is declared but never enforced in the loop. A's diagnosis of the rounding problem and its NEEDS_HUMAN prompt exit are a bit richer, but that does not quite make up for the gaps in its stopping conditions.
